[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided a breakdown of the weathering process into three main categories: dirt and grime, fading and wear, and rust and corrosion.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For dirt and grime, the assistant recommended using pigment powders (e.g., Vallejo, Mig Productions, or AK Interactive), washes (e.g., Citadel Shade, Vallejo Wash, or AK Interactive Wash), and drybrushing with acrylic paints or pigments.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For fading and wear, the assistant suggested using acrylic paints (e.g., Vallejo, Tamiya, or Mr. Hobby), enamel paints (e.g., Tamiya or Testors), and chipping mediums (e.g., Vallejo Chipping Medium or AK Interactive Chipping Fluid).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For rust and corrosion, the assistant recommended using rust-colored pigments or paints (e.g., Vallejo, AK Interactive, or Mig Productions) and rust effects products (e.g., Vallejo Rust Effect or AK Interactive Rust).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant mentioned popular weathering products and brands, including Vallejo, AK Interactive, Mig Productions, and Citadel.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant advised starting with a smaller, more subtle effect and building up gradually, experimenting on a test model, and practicing to achieve a realistic look.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant emphasized that the key to realistic weathering is subtlety and warned against overdoing it.

[USER] The user asked about the difference between Vallejo pigments and washes and when to use each.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant explained that Vallejo Pigments are finely ground powders used for surface effects like dirt, grime, and rust, while Vallejo Washes are thinned, translucent acrylic paints used for shading and enhancing details.
